messages.content: Prepare a notice in French for volunteers about picking up supply kits in Room 4 on Saturday. Give me the headline first. I’ll send the pickup time in a separate turn before you draft the two-sentence notice.
Where are we? Pickup is at 10 a.m. Saturday.
Actually, pickup is at 11 a.m. Continue with the corrected notice.
Prepare a two-sentence notice asking volunteers to bring gloves to the yard cleanup on Saturday. Give me only a headline first. Wait for me to request the body.
Cancel the cleanup notice. We won’t publish it.
New task. Write a single-sentence thank-you to the volunteers who sorted supplies on Friday.

I’m choosing between a single sentence and two short sentences for a narrow visitor sign. The sign needs to say that visitors must leave backpacks at the desk before entering the exhibit. Recommend a format. Wait to write the sign until I ask.
What would make two short sentences a better choice?
Use two short sentences. Write the sign now.
The project note from last month lists Room 12 as the usual supply pickup location. Tell me which room the note lists before I send you this week’s location.
This Saturday’s pickup is in Room 4. That’s a one-time change. Draft a one-sentence notice for Saturday.
The desk just verified that Saturday’s pickup has moved again, to Room 6. Correct the Saturday line and give me a separate, one-sentence reminder for the usual weekly pickup.
